d: Humanity’s five solar-escape probes and their future stellar encounter destinations.

voyager-1.x: Crossed the heliopause into interstellar space in 2012; heading toward a 1.6-ly flyby of Gliese 445 in ~40,000 years.

voyager-2.x: Crossed the heliopause into interstellar space in 2018; heading toward a 1.7-ly flyby of Ross 248 in ~42,000 years.

pioneer-10.x: First spacecraft to traverse the Asteroid Belt and encounter Jupiter (1973); drifting toward Aldebaran over ~2 million years.

pioneer-11.x: First spacecraft to encounter Saturn (1979); escaping the Solar System toward the constellation Scutum and Aquila.

new-horizons.x: Fifth solar-escape spacecraft; conducted flybys of Pluto (2015) and Kuiper Belt contact binary 486958 Arrokoth (2019).

gaia-1129149723913123456.x: M-dwarf 17.6 light-years away; Voyager 1 will make its closest approach (1.6 ly) in ~40,000 years.

gaia-1926461164913660160.x: Red dwarf 10.3 light-years away; Voyager 2 will pass within 1.7 light-years in ~42,000 years.

hip-21421.x: Orange giant 65 light-years away toward which Pioneer 10 is drifting over the next two million years.

gaia-5853498713190525696.x: Target of the Breakthrough Starshot relativistic laser-sail nanocraft concept and the 1988 USNA/NASA Project Longshot nuclear-pulse study.

gaia-4472832130942575872.x: Target of the landmark 1973–1978 British Interplanetary Society Project Daedalus two-stage fusion interstellar probe study.

b.s: Deep-space probes escaping the Solar System on hyperbolic trajectories (Voyager 1 & 2, Pioneer 10 & 11, New Horizons) and their distant stellar encounters.
b.r: NASA JPL Horizons & Bailer-Jones et al. (2019) Gaia DR2 Stellar Encounters
